# EDA 

## Dataset Overview

```{r}
# install packages, should only run once
# install.packages(c("readr", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "tidyr", "lubridate", "zoo"),
#                   repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(lubridate)
library(zoo)
library(knitr)
```

```{r}
main_data_self <- readRDS("data/processed/main_data_self.rds")
main_data_official <- readRDS("data/processed/main_data_official.rds")
extended_data_self <- readRDS("data/processed/extended_data_self.rds")
extended_data_official <- readRDS("data/processed/extended_data_official.rds")
```

```{r}
datasets <- list(
  main_data_self = main_data_self,
  main_data_official = main_data_official,
  extended_data_self = extended_data_self,
  extended_data_official = extended_data_official
)

overview <- bind_rows(lapply(names(datasets), function(nm) {
  df <- datasets[[nm]]

  data.frame(
    dataset = nm,
    observations = nrow(df),
    variables = ncol(df),
    start = min(df$date),
    end = max(df$date),
    missing = sum(is.na(df))
  )
}))

print(overview)
```

```{r}
data.frame(
  dataset = c("Main", "Extended"),
  predictors = c(
    sum(startsWith(names(main_data_self), "CAN_")),
    sum(startsWith(names(extended_data_self), "CAN_")) +
      sum(startsWith(names(extended_data_self), "US_"))
  )
)
```

```{r}
missing_count <- colSums(is.na(extended_data_self))
missing_count[missing_count > 0]
```

```{r}
missing_count <- colSums(is.na(extended_data_official))
missing_count[missing_count > 0]
```

```{r}
extended_data_official %>%
  filter(is.na(US_ACOGNO)) %>%
  select(date, US_ACOGNO)

extended_data_self %>%
  filter(is.na(US_ACOGNO)) %>%
  select(date, US_ACOGNO)
```

`US_ACOGNO` missing values are from 1981-01-01 to 1992-01-01. From 1992-02-01 onwards, there is data for `US_ACOGNO`, except for 2026-07-01. The disparity in missing values for official and self data is from this variable (difference = 132). 

```{r}
missing_by_month <- extended_data_official %>%
  select(date, starts_with("US_")) %>%
  mutate(
    missing_count = rowSums(
      is.na(across(starts_with("US_")))
    )
  ) %>%
  select(date, missing_count) %>%
  filter(missing_count > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(missing_count))

print(missing_by_month, n = Inf)
```

```{r}
missing_by_month <- extended_data_self %>%
  select(date, starts_with("US_")) %>%
  mutate(
    missing_count = rowSums(
      is.na(across(starts_with("US_")))
    )
  ) %>%
  select(date, missing_count) %>%
  filter(missing_count > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(missing_count))

print(missing_by_month, n = Inf)
```

```{r}
us_cols <- grep(
  "^US_",
  names(extended_data_official),
  value = TRUE
)

us_data <- extended_data_official %>%
  select(date, all_of(us_cols))

missing_by_variable <- colSums(
  is.na(us_data[, us_cols, drop = FALSE])
)

fred_summary <- data.frame(
  Measure = c(
    "Total US predictors",
    "Complete US predictors",
    "Predictors with missing values",
    "Maximum missing observations per predictor",
    "Months with at least one missing predictor"
  ),
  Value = c(
    length(us_cols),
    sum(missing_by_variable == 0),
    sum(missing_by_variable > 0),
    max(missing_by_variable),
    sum(rowSums(is.na(
      us_data[, us_cols, drop = FALSE]
    )) > 0)
  )
)

kable(
  fred_summary,
  caption = "Table A2. FRED-MD Missingness Summary"
)
```

## Descriptive statistics for inflation

```{r}
p_inflation <- main_data_official %>%
  filter(!is.na(inflation_mom)) %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(date, inflation_mom * 100)
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dotted"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = as.Date("2012-02-01"),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "firebrick"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Canadian Monthly CPI Inflation",
    subtitle = "Official seasonally adjusted CPI",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Monthly log inflation (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p_inflation)
```

```{r}
inflation_stats <- main_data_official %>%
  filter(!is.na(inflation_mom)) %>%
  mutate(
    inflation_pct = inflation_mom * 100,
    period = case_when(
      date < as.Date("2012-02-01") ~ "1992-2012", # until jan 2012 
      date < as.Date("2020-01-01") ~ "2012-2019", # until feb 2012 
      TRUE ~ "2020-2026"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    Mean = mean(inflation_pct),
    SD = sd(inflation_pct),
    Min = min(inflation_pct),
    Max = max(inflation_pct),
    AC1 = cor(
      inflation_pct[-1],
      inflation_pct[-length(inflation_pct)]
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(
  inflation_stats,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Descriptive Statistics of Canadian Monthly Inflation"
)
```

```{r}
# descriptive statistics 
inflation_stats <- inflation_compare %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -date,
    names_to = "series",
    values_to = "inflation"
  ) %>%
  group_by(series) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(inflation, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(inflation, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(inflation, na.rm = TRUE),
    min = min(inflation, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(inflation, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(inflation_stats)
```

We plot autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation to examine our inflation variables. 

```{r}
# comparing across same time periods (starting from 1992)
start_date <- as.Date("1992-01-01")
end_date <- as.Date("2012-02-01")

self_common <- main_data_self %>%
  filter(date >= start_date, date <= end_date)

official_common <- main_data_official %>%
  filter(date >= start_date, date <= end_date)

inflation_common <- main_data_self %>%
  select(date, self = inflation_mom) %>%
  inner_join(
    main_data_official %>%
      select(date, official = inflation_mom),
    by = "date"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    date <= end_date,
    complete.cases(self, official)
  )

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

acf(inflation_common$self, lag.max = 36,
    main = "ACF: Self-adjusted")

pacf(inflation_common$self, lag.max = 36,
     main = "PACF: Self-adjusted")

acf(inflation_common$official, lag.max = 36,
    main = "ACF: Official")

pacf(inflation_common$official, lag.max = 36,
     main = "PACF: Official")
```

Interpretation: 
- similar autocorrelation structures between self-adjusted and official CPI 
- both exhibit weak overall autocorrelation with a large negative correlation at lag 12 and a few isolated PACF spikes 
- Implications
  - supprts AR models, but AR(1) is not necessarily sufficient -- should use BIC or validation to choose best model, similar to Mederios et al. methodology 
  - similarity strengthens our confidence in self-adjusted CPI 

## Rolling volatility 
Does inflation volatility change across economic periods? 

```{r}
volatility_official <- main_data_official %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  mutate(
    rolling_sd_12 = zoo::rollapply(
      inflation_mom,
      width = 12,
      FUN = sd,
      fill = NA,
      align = "right"
    )
  )

ggplot(volatility_official, aes(date, rolling_sd_12 * 100)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = as.Date("2012-02-01"),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "firebrick"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "12-Month Rolling Volatility of Canadian Inflation (Officially-adjusted CPI)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Rolling SD (monthly percentage points)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
